accepted.hypothesis: D07 (2,6-dichloro-BQ) has f=1.24 but O2 margin only 0.097. D08 (F4) has a higher margin of 0.178 while keeping f=1.03. Adding one F should lift the margin above 0.15 without the f loss seen with heavier halogenation (D14 f=0.72, D11 f=0.28). Aiming for f>=2 is a stretch. This is the minimal-risk test of whether an F raises the margin on the Cl2 scaffold.

This mixes the two f-positive motifs, Cl at 2,6 (D07 f=1.24) and F at 3,5 (D08 f=1.03). The aim is to keep f>0 while pushing the margin toward or above 0.15, since D08 and D14 show halogen count raises the margin. Fluorine is smaller than Br, so it should not repeat the f penalty of D11. CN is avoided because every CN reference detached CO2.

accepted.hypothesis: D08 (F4-BQ) is f-positive with margin 0.178 and no detachment. D14 (Cl4) has a higher margin of 0.346 but lower f. A single Cl swap on the F4 scaffold should keep most of the F4 f value while gaining some margin. It tests whether a small amount of Cl is a favorable trade-off. Because D07 shows Cl-bearing BQs can have f above 1, I expect f to stay above 1.

Br gave the largest O2 margin in the set (D11, 0.462, no detachment). D07's margin is only 0.097. Placing Br at 3,5 on the Cl2 scaffold should raise the margin well above 0.15. The risk is that heavier halogens lowered f (D11 f=0.28 versus D08 f=1.03), so f>=2 is unlikely. This probes the margin-versus-f edge of the tradeoff, and DFT will show whether the Cl2 core keeps f from collapsing.

D15 (phenanthrenequinone) has f=1.09, the best non-halogenated f, but its margin is -0.196. Chlorination raised the margin of AQ-type and NQ-type cores by about 0.28 (D12 -0.191 to D13 0.089). Chlorinating both outer rings should bring D15's margin up substantially while retaining the ortho-quinone geometry that favors f. NH2 and OH are avoided because they lowered f in D01, D04 and D05.

accepted.hypothesis: Adding F to the D07 Cl2 scaffold raised f from 1.24 to 1.32-1.38, while heavier halogens (Br, D11 f=0.28; Cl4, D14 f=0.72) lowered it. Swapping both Cl for F should keep the strong CO2 binding of the 2,6-disubstituted BQ (D07 bind -25.8 kcal/mol) with a smaller steric footprint. The F4 core D08 has margin 0.178, so margin should rise above D07's 0.097. Aiming for f>=2 is a stretch, and this tests whether less halogen mass helps f.

D08 (F4) has f=1.03, margin 0.178 and no detachment. D07, with two ring H atoms, has the higher f of 1.24. Removing one F leaves a trifluoro-BQ with one H, to test whether an open ring site raises f toward D07's level while F keeps the margin above 0.15. Heavier halogenation lowered f (D14, D11), so I expect f to rise as halogen count falls.

accepted.hypothesis: A mixed F2Cl2 pattern with Cl and F alternating around the ring. The nearby F2Cl2 isomers had f=1.32 (margin 0.26) and f=1.17 (margin 0.22), both with no detachment. This is a new substitution pattern, in which Cl at the para-related positions retains the Cl-driven binding of D07 and F keeps f up. Mixed F/Cl has never lowered f below 1.1 in the history. It probes whether the pattern gives a margin above 0.15 with f>1.3.

D15 (phenanthrenequinone) has f=1.09 and bind -27.9 kcal/mol, the strongest CO2 binding, but its margin is -0.196. Dichlorination (2,7) raised the margin to -0.017 but lowered f to 0.82. Chlorinating only one outer ring should cost less f, since the first Cl gives most of the benefit per halogen. Margin should rise by about half of the dichloro gain, which probably still falls short of 0.15. It tests the f/margin trade-off on the ortho-quinone core, and the margin is the risk here.

rejected.hypothesis: Monofluorination of D07 (f 1.24 to 1.38) and difluorination (f 1.32) both raised f and margin. Here one Cl is removed and two F are added, giving a mono-Cl difluoro-BQ with one open H. This reduces heavy-halogen load, which lowered f in D14 and D11, while the F pair raises the margin toward 0.18-0.26. It tests whether Cl count is the lever for f at fixed F.

accepted.hypothesis: D15 has the strongest CO2 binding (-27.9 kcal/mol) and f=1.09, but a margin of -0.196. Monochlorination lowered the margin penalty only to -0.106 and cost little f (1.04), while dichlorination lowered f to 0.82. F is the halogen that raised f in the BQ series (F2 compound 1.65 vs Cl2 1.24), so one F on the ortho-quinone core should give a similar margin gain with a smaller f cost. The margin will probably stay below 0.15. This tests whether F is better than Cl on this core.

rejected.hypothesis: Replacing both Cl on D07 with F raised f from 1.24 to 1.65, so F is the f-promoting halogen. Here I take D08 (F4, f=1.03) and remove two F to give 2,5-difluoro-BQ, the para-disposed isomer of the 2,6-F2 compound. I expect f to rise as halogen count falls, as the D08 to trifluoro to F2 trend suggests. Margin should be near 0 to 0.1, so the margin is the risk. This tests whether the para arrangement lifts the margin without losing f. F4-BQ (K084) is a known CO2 adduct former.

Margin will likely be negative, since the F2 compound dropped to -0.03. It tests the f end of the tradeoff, and DFT will decide whether f>=2 is reachable. The BQ core is a documented CO2 adduct former (K026).
